title: One-Pot Creamy Cabbage & White Bean Noodles
description: Tender cabbage, white beans, and noodles cook together into a mild, creamy pantry dinner with no specialty ingredients.
equipment: large pot or deep skillet with lid
substitutions: Use chickpeas instead of white beans.
Use Monterey Jack instead of cheddar.
Use small pasta shapes if you do not have egg noodles.

steps.text: Cook the cabbage and noodles together.

cookSteps.text: Put 4 cups sliced cabbage, 3 cups broth, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder if using in a large pot. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook 5 minutes to start softening the cabbage.
Stir in 8 ounces egg noodles. Cook uncovered, stirring often, for about 8 minutes or until the noodles are tender. Add a small splash of water if the pot gets dry before the noodles are done.
Stir in 1 drained 15-ounce can white beans and 3/4 cup milk. Cook 3–4 minutes, stirring, until the beans are hot and the sauce is creamy.
Remove from the heat and stir in 3/4 cup shredded cheddar until melted. Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat gently with a splash of milk or broth until steaming hot.

title: Turkey, Apple & Cheddar Skillet Melts
description: Deli turkey, crisp apple, and cheddar turn ordinary bread into a warm skillet lunch in about 15 minutes.
substitutions: Use a pear instead of apple.
Use mayonnaise instead of mustard or leave it out.

steps.text: Build the turkey, apple, and cheddar sandwiches.

cookSteps.text: Lay out 4 slices bread. Spread 2 teaspoons mustard over the inside faces if using. Divide 6 ounces deli turkey, 1/2 thinly sliced apple, and 4 slices cheddar between 2 sandwiches.
Spread the outsides of the sandwiches with 1 tablespoon softened butter total.
Heat a large skillet over medium-low. Cook the sandwiches 3–4 minutes per side, pressing gently, until the bread is golden and the cheddar is melted.
Let the melts stand 1 minute, then cut and serve.

storage: Best eaten right away. Refrigerate any leftover cooked sandwich up to 2 days and reheat in a skillet or toaster oven until hot.

title: Leftover Roasted Vegetable & Cheddar Pasta
description: Leftover roasted vegetables become a fast creamy pasta instead of disappearing into the back of the fridge.
substitutions: Use cooked rice instead of pasta and warm everything in a skillet.
Use Monterey Jack instead of cheddar.
Any mix of roasted broccoli, carrots, cauliflower, zucchini, potatoes, or peppers works.

steps.text: Warm the vegetables and make the quick cheese sauce.

cookSteps.text: Cook 6 ounces short pasta in boiling salted water according to the package directions until tender, about 8–10 minutes. Before draining, scoop out 1/4 cup pasta water.
Drain the pasta and return it to the pot with 2 cups chopped leftover roasted vegetables, 1/2 cup milk, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder if using.
Cook over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until the vegetables are steaming hot.
Remove from the heat and stir in 3/4 cup shredded cheddar. Add a little reserved pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce. Season to taste and serve.

storage: Use vegetables only while they are still within their original safe refrigerated storage window. Refrigerate the finished pasta up to 3 days and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Small-Batch Caramel Banana Bread Cups
description: One ripe banana makes six soft little banana bread cups with a simple brown-sugar caramel drizzle.

ingredients.item: heavy cream or milk for sauce

substitutions: Use milk instead of heavy cream for a lighter, thinner sauce.
Leave out the cinnamon if you prefer plain banana flavor.
Use neutral oil instead of melted butter in the batter.

steps.text: Mix and bake six banana cups.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease 6 cups of a muffin pan.
Mash 1 large ripe banana. Stir in 1 egg, 1/4 cup melted butter or oil, and 1/4 cup brown sugar until combined.
Stir in 3/4 cup flour, 1/2 teaspoon baking powder, and 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon if using just until no dry flour remains. Divide among 6 muffin cups.
Bake 16–18 minutes, until the tops spring back lightly and a toothpick comes out without wet batter.

While the cups cool, put 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 2 tablespoons heavy cream or milk, and 1 tablespoon butter in a small saucepan. Bring to a gentle bubble over medium-low heat and stir for 1–2 minutes until smooth.
Spoon the warm brown-sugar sauce over the banana cups and serve.

storage: Store the banana cups covered at room temperature for 2 days or refrigerate up to 5 days. Refrigerate leftover sauce and warm it gently before serving.
